text:
alexm: heads up — seeing apiserver circuiting in eu-west1 for ~30s every 3-5m since 08:10 UTC. coincides with massive GPU onboarding bursts from the provisioner :thinking:

jamie: same, graphs show watch lat p50 -> p95 explosion and apiserver 503 spikes. link: https://grafana.internal/r/abc123 (eu-west1) :eyes:

sre-oncall-bot: ALERT: APISERVER_503_SPIKE eu-west1 (08:12 UTC) — spike duration 32s, impact ~12% of requests :rotating_light:

kevin: pulled etcd leader history — looks like leader epoch flips and short term jumps around the same times. snippet:
```
# etcdctl --endpoints=https://etcd-eu-west1:2379 endpoint status --write-out=table
ENDPOINT           ID               VERSION   LEADER    RAFT TERM  RAFT INDEX
https://10.0.1.3   b3a2d4f9         3.5.2     0x8a7b    14         1234567
https://10.0.1.4   c5f4b6a1         3.5.2     0x8a7b    17         1234570
# note: term mismatch spikes (14->17) around 08:10
```

maria: likely cause: provisioner onboarding kicks lots of new nodes which open persistent watches (kubelet -> apiserver -> etcd watch fanout). apiserver circuit-breaker trips then some controllers retry aggressively. that amplifies leader flips.

carol: agreed. short-term mitigations we can apply now: 1) throttle onboarding in provisioner (reduce batch size), 2) cordon/taint new nodes to slow kubelet registration, 3) temporarily increase apiserver --max-mutating-requests-inflight and --max-requests-inflight to raise capacity, 4) increase apiserver client QPS for controller-manager.

alexm: we need to be careful with increasing inflight limits — may worsen etcd leader churn if backend can't keep up. but we need something that reduces immediate 503s. cost question: should we bump reserved GPU pool to avoid bursting the provisioner? that has $$ implications.

jamie: for immediate relief I'll cordon a chunk of onboarding nodes and add a label so provisioner stops draining more into eu-west1. doing:
```
kubectl get nodes -l onboarding=true -o name | head -n 20 | xargs -n1 kubectl cordon
kubectl label nodes -l onboarding=true throttle=onboarding-pause
```

kevin: also running quick etcd health checks and defrag schedule on standby members. recommending we run defrag outside peak and bump etcd snapshot retention threshold temporarily: check metrics server_leader_changes_total and send alert if > 3 in 5m.

maria: I'll open a PR to provisioner to reduce batch size EU-west from 40->8 and add jitter between batches. that'll take ~30m to review. also proposing a reserved pool of 24 GPUs for critical workloads so we don't autoscale aggressively into apiserver limits. cost estimate: +$13k/month for reserved pool in eu-west1.

carol: medium-term: add rate-limiter in node-register path, and add backpressure signal from apiserver (429 propagation) so provisioner slows. Also consider adding a separate control-plane endpoint for onboarding-heavy clusters (or route to Dedicated controlplane in extreme cases).

alexm: can someone post the kube-apiserver logs for one of the 503 windows? need the circuit-breaker traces.

jamie: pasted minimal excerpt:
```
I0311 08:10:12.345678 1 wrap.go:47] apiserver: timeout waiting for watch connection
I0311 08:10:12.345680 1 request.go:123] client 10.4.2.7: request took 1234ms and failed: 503 "apiserver circuit open"
I0311 08:10:44.512233 1 trace.go:85] TRACE: watch-fanout handled 1400 watchers in 2.3s
```

kevin: that TRACE matches the etcd term jumps — backend IO is getting saturated during the bursts. check NVMe iops and etcd WAL_latency metrics.

maria: actionable steps:
- jamie: cordon nodes (done) ✅
- kevin: run etcd health check + defrag plan ⏳
- carol: prepare temp config bump for apiserver inflight only if etcd metrics stable 👀
- I'll open PR to throttle provisioner and a ticket for reserved pool cost analysis

carol: I'll also temporarily reduce controller-manager leader election renewDeadline to speed failover if leader flaps? note: risky. maybe better to reduce retries in specific controllers (node controller).

alexm: thanks team. create incident and put a brief runbook update for onboarding->apiserver coupling. let's reconvene in 45m and decide on reserved pool purchase if PR looks good.

sre-oncall-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-1123 "eu-west1 apiserver circuiting during GPU onboarding" — assigned to eng-sre 📝

jamie: brief note — after cordoning first batch, 503 spike amplitude dropped ~60% in next window. monitoring.

kevin: posting one-liner commands i used for checks:
```
etcdctl endpoint status --write-out=table
kubectl top nodes --selector=onboarding=true
journalctl -u kube-apiserver --since "10 minutes ago" | grep -E "503|circuit|watch"
```

maria: thanks — I'll include cost + mitigation plan in the incident ticket.

alexm: closing loop: if we still see leader term jumps after throttling, escalate to infra for NVMe IO increase or move etcd to a larger instance class. 👍

carol: noted. prepping a short runbook entry for node-onboard backpressure and apiserver knobs.

alexm: good job. monitoring handoff to nightshift. :)
file_creation_note: incident-style thread about apiserver 503s during GPU onboarding; includes commands, short actions, and cost tradeoffs
